channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [7] Emergent partons in fractional quantum Hall systems
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Ajit C. Balram, Lingjie Du

Authors: Zihao Yang, Yifan Wang, Xinyu Lu, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental evidence for partons in fractional quantum Hall systems, relevant to strongly correlated electrons.

Tags: #fractionalquantumHall #stronglycorrelated #experiment

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03338-9 In a geometrical theory for the fractional quantum Hall effect, chiral spin-2 neutral excitations arise. Now, multiple such excitations are observed and provide evidence for the parton description of the quantum Hall effect.

item.title: [9] Microscopic signatures of an imaginary charge density wave in a kagome metal
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: H. Kontani, Y. Matsuda

Authors: S. Suetsugu, F. Hori, M. Shibata, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: kagome metal

Tags: #kagome #CsV3Sb5 #V3Sb5 #chargedensitywave #loopcurrent #time-reversalsymmetrybreaking

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03339-8 Whether imaginary charge density waves and their associated loop currents exist has remained an open question. Now signatures of this state have been observed in kagome metal CsV3Sb5, revealing spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking.
